item.title: J&J Snack Foods Targets Additional Cost Savings Under Project Apollo 2
item.description: Chief Executive Dan Fachner stated that the company's turnaround plan remains on schedule following a strong fiscal year. The Project Apollo initiative yielded over 25 million dollars in permanent savings, with an additional phase planned through 2027.

item.title: Nvidia Shares Drop 14% to Mark Longest Weekly Slide Since 2008
item.description: The chipmaker concluded its longest stretch of consecutive weekly losses since the 2008 financial crisis. After previously holding the top spot globally by valuation, the firm now trails Apple, Microsoft, and Alphabet.

item.title: Dow and S&P 500 Reach Correction Territory as Tech Leads Broad Drop
item.description: The Dow and S&P 500 slid into a market correction as the Nasdaq marked its sharpest weekly contraction since 2020. Every major industry group within the S&P 500 dropped by more than 1% during the week.

item.title: Semiconductor Stocks Shed $2.3 Trillion in Worst Week in 25 Years
item.description: A primary index tracking semiconductor equities recorded its largest weekly loss in a quarter of a century. The decline wiped out 2.3 trillion dollars in market value amid a broader retreat from artificial intelligence investments.

item.title: S&P 500 Suffers Widespread Losses as 94% of Index Components Drop
item.description: Almost the entire S&P 500 finished the week lower, with eleven constituent equities losing at least a fifth of their value. Despite the sharp drawdown, Wall Street analysts maintain that buying these shares could still yield strong returns.

item.title: CVC Marathon's Bruce Richards Cautions on Irrational Markets and Leveraged ETFs
item.description: Bruce Richards shared his perspectives on maintaining liquidity during an interview on Bloomberg Money. The managing partner raised concerns about irrational trading behavior and expressed skepticism toward leveraged exchange-traded funds.

item.title: Trump Threatens Heavy Tax on U.S. Companies Building Data Centers Abroad
item.description: President Trump pledged to block domestic firms from constructing data center facilities in foreign countries. He delivered the warning at the White House following a summit in China with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.

item.title: Corporate Share Issuance Rises as Anthropic Prepares $81 Billion IPO
item.description: Corporations are shifting away from repurchasing equity and are instead issuing new shares to the market. This incoming supply will face a major test from Anthropic's planned 81 billion dollar public offering.

item.title: Sophisticated AI Cyberattacks Trigger Surge in Japanese Insurance Claims
item.description: Major property insurers in Japan are experiencing a substantial increase in cyber insurance payouts. The trend is being driven by higher volumes of nationwide hacking incidents and more advanced artificial intelligence techniques.

item.title: Anthropic IPO Debuts as Analysts Caution Over Near-Term Volatility
item.description: Anthropic has completed an initial public offering described as a necessary boost for public markets. Market analysts caution that trading in the company's shares is likely to remain unstable over the coming weeks.

item.title: Japanese Yen Leads G-10 Currencies Amid Broad Technology Stock Slump
item.description: The yen outpaced all other Group of 10 currencies during Friday's trading session. Demand for the safe-haven currency expanded as equity declines across technology shares spread into Asian markets.

item.title: Senate Passes BAAJA Permitting Reform Supported by AI and Energy
item.description: Legislation aimed at permitting reform has successfully advanced through the Senate with backing from energy and artificial intelligence industries. To be enacted into law, the measure must now secure approval in the House before reaching President Trump.

item.title: AMD Drops Over 7% Following Short Seller Allegations on China Exposure
item.description: Shares fell sharply after a short seller claimed the chipmaker's firmware was found at an entity on a U.S. blacklist. The company responded by stating that it remains in full compliance with United States law.

item.title: Anthropic IPO Draws Retail Interest Without Lifting Broader Tech Market
item.description: Individual retail traders actively participated in Anthropic's public offering. Despite this participation, the debut did not trigger a wider rally across the technology sector.

item.title: Cybersecurity Stocks Gain While Broad S&P 500 Suffers Sharp Thursday Selloff
item.description: A broad equity downturn pulled down all 11 sectors within the S&P 500 during Thursday's session. Ten of those sectors lost more than 1%, while cybersecurity shares managed to resist the broader drop.

item.title: Intuit Issues Downbeat Forecast Adding to Legacy Software Sector Concerns
item.description: The TurboTax producer released a weaker outlook that troubled investors on Wall Street. The softer forecast amplified broader market worries surrounding established legacy software providers.

item.title: Global Equities Face Steepest Losing Run Since 2023 as AI Trade Slides
item.description: Worldwide share benchmarks headed toward their longest decline in over three years following an unwinding in AI-related equities. Capital moved toward traditional safe havens, driving demand into U.S. Treasuries.

item.title: Copper Prices Recover Following Recent Sell-Off
item.description: Copper prices saw a partial rebound after a significant decline on Wednesday. Market participants are questioning if the recent sell-off driven by AI and tariff concerns was excessive.

item.title: Palo Alto Networks Raises Outlook Amid AI Demand
item.description: Palo Alto Networks increased its financial outlook following recent earnings results. Management cited the current threat landscape as a driver for future demand.

item.title: Palo Alto Networks Acquires Applied Compute for $4.5 Billion
item.description: Palo Alto Networks announced a $4.5 billion acquisition of AI startup Applied Compute. Shares of the company rose 7% following the announcement and earnings report.

item.title: Nvidia Interim CEO Kress Addresses Staff Following Huang Departure
item.description: Interim CEO Colette Kress held her first all-hands meeting to encourage employees to move forward. The leadership transition follows the exit of former CEO Jensen Huang.

item.title: Death Cross Pattern Emerges in Small-Cap Stocks
item.description: A technical 'death cross' pattern has appeared in small-cap stocks. This indicator suggests potential weakness within the Russell 2000 index.

item.title: Oil Prices Stabilize Amid Geopolitical Tensions
item.description: Oil prices remained steady as market participants monitored the conflict between the US and Iran. Traders are evaluating the potential for further escalations involving Tehran.

item.title: Copper Supply Concerns May Impact AI Infrastructure
item.description: A recent decline in copper prices raises concerns about the long-term availability of the metal for AI infrastructure. Future mining output may struggle to keep pace with projected demand.

item.title: Anthropic May Increase IPO Offering Amid Strong Investor Interest
item.description: The AI company is reportedly considering a larger share offering due to high demand. Trading on the Nasdaq is scheduled to commence this Thursday.

item.title: Ed Yardeni Views Current Interest Rates as 'Normal for Longer'
item.description: Market researcher Ed Yardeni suggests that interest rates will remain at current levels rather than rising further. This perspective follows a period of inconsistent signals from central bank officials regarding the pace of future hikes.

item.title: Gopinath Notes Alignment Between Warsh and Waller on Fed Policy
item.description: Gita Gopinath suggests that Fed Chair Kevin Warsh shares a similar policy outlook to Governor Christopher Waller. Waller has explicitly advocated for a 50-basis-point rate hike in December.

item.title: Investors Pay Premium for Defensive Stocks Despite High Valuations
item.description: Market participants are favoring defensive sectors that have outperformed the S&P 500 recently. These stocks are trading at higher valuations relative to earnings estimates than the broader index.

item.title: Analyst Suggests Oracle Shares Remain Undervalued
item.description: Bernstein analysts argue that Oracle's stock price is low even under pessimistic business scenarios. The valuation remains attractive even if the company's AI data-center segment were to fail.

item.title: Nvidia Faces Uncertainty Despite Strong AI Demand
item.description: While demand for Nvidia products remains high, investors are concerned about several strategic risks. Key issues include leadership transition, export regulations, and market exposure to China.
